purpose: Teach: 漱石/空軍/レジャー/ヘリコプター/スタディ/ベクトル/マンハッタン/マダム

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは漱石を読んでらしたぞ
lines.en: You know, when your father was young, he used to read Soseki.
lines.style: Quiet, gentle opening. Soft gaze into the middle distance. Pace unhurried, like watching a memory surface. Voice carries the weight of time — not sad, just tender with distance.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、空軍の方とお話されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh yes, dear — and you talked with that air force fellow, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, conspiratorial. A knowing smile in the voice. She's following his thread but gently correcting the record. Playful tease underneath — she remembers differently. Soft, quick cadence.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんとレジャーランドに行ったぞ
lines.en: When your father was young, we went to the amusement park together.
lines.style: Same wistful anchor, but lighter now. A small smile in the voice. Less weight, more accessibility — he's sharing something less serious. Still slow, still sparing with words.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ヘリコプターの音に驚かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh, but you were startled by the helicopter noise, weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Affectionate correction again. She's not letting him drift into his version — she has hers. Light laugh underneath. Bright, quick, like she's been waiting to remind him of this.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがケーススタディを学ばれたぞ
lines.en: When your father was young, he studied case analysis.
lines.style: Back to the wistful register. Slight weight again — he's moved to something more formal, more serious. Pause before 'studied' — gathering the memory. Steady, low voice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、数学のベクトルに苦戦されてたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh, but you struggled with vectors in mathematics, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: She's playfully contradicting him again — with love. A knowing chuckle in the voice. She's the keeper of the real story. Bouncy, slightly conspiratorial, like she's enjoyed holding onto this particular truth.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはマンハッタンの記事を読まれたぞ
lines.en: When your father was young, he read an article about Manhattan.
lines.style: The wistfulness returns, almost philosophical now. Slower pace. The detail of Manhattan carries a particular weight — some longing in it, some distance. Voice thins slightly on the trailing words.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、上品なマダムにご挨拶されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you greeted that refined woman so gracefully, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Final warm correction. Voice closes gently — almost a benediction. She's been waiting to say this. Tender, satisfied, a soft smile held in the voice. Slight fadeout, intimate.
